units.title: TPM and recovery qualification, then LUKS2 by default and TPM auto-unlock where safe
units.note: L-002 and L-003 are blocked on L-001, and L-001 is NOT finished. TWO GATES THIS NOTE ONCE NAMED ARE NOW MET AND NEITHER WAS ENOUGH. Round 31 (unit later-silicon) did a real enrol-and-recover cycle on silicon; round 32 (unit later-silicon-2, 2026-09-19, commit 16fe7ad3) CLEARED KATANA'S TPM with Andre's explicit approval and showed tpm-unlock=REFUSED -> recovery-unlock=SUCCESS -> marker identical in one boot on an Intel PTT fTPM. Do NOT read either as grounds to unblock anything. L-001 stays partial at 4 of 5 runs: Run 5, the TPM-removed case, needs a hand in firmware setup because PPI operation 2 takes /sys/class/tpm/tpm0/ppi with it and re-enabling is not symmetric with disabling; Run 3 has no firmware capsule to apply. L-002 stays blocked because installer/apex-install still cannot create a LUKS header at all, and because systemd-cryptenroll's default on systemd 258.10 binds to NO PCRs, so a naive 'encrypt by default' would seal to the SRK and nothing else. L-003 stays blocked because systemd-pcrextend is a silent no-op (exit 0, PCR 11 unchanged) on a GRUB machine, so the signed PCR 11 policy cannot be satisfied at boot on a default APEX install - that needs the sd-stub/UKI path, not the Secure Boot switch. Turning on full-disk encryption by default without a proven recovery path is how a user loses everything. AND A HARDWARE RULE FOR ANYONE WHO TOUCHES KATANA: /dev/nvme0n1 IS NOT A STABLE NAME THERE. The two NVMe controllers are probed asynchronously. Round 32 logged three boots: the first two enumerated them one way and the third - an ORDINARY reboot, not the clear - enumerated them the other way, so the disk this programme is told never to write became the APEX disk. Identify by serial (Micron_2450 220534D1CB81 = APEX, SPCC M.2 240023925111005 = Windows), by PCI function (0000:03:00.0 = APEX, 0000:02:00.0 = Windows), by PARTUUID, or by label (apex-root / EFI-SYSTEM / games). And APEX's default boot entry Boot0000 lives on the WINDOWS disk's ESP (PARTUUID 2ba9a2ea), the same partition Windows Boot Manager boots from.
units.closed: CLOSED TO DISPATCH 2026-09-19 (round 32). Round 31 asked Andre whether katana's TPM could be cleared; HE SAID YES, and unit later-silicon-2 ran Run 2 on branch task/later-silicon-2 (commit 16fe7ad3, pushed, cut from roadmap/v2.2 f602f1cb). Evidence: ROADMAP/evidence/L-001-katana-tpm-20260919.md sections 14-21. THE CLEAR HAPPENED AND WAS VERIFIED FIVE WAYS rather than inferred from the reboot - lockoutAuthSet 1->0, five persistent handles->none, thirteen NV indices->five, four NV counters->zero, DA counter 2->0 well before its first decay step. A volume enrolled BEFORE the clear then gave tpm-unlock=REFUSED -> recovery-unlock=SUCCESS -> recovery-marker=MATCH in ONE BOOT. The authorised cost was Andre's Windows Hello PIN; there is no BitLocker, so no data. L-001 IS NOW 4 OF 5 RUNS AND STAYS partial. WHAT IS LEFT IS STILL NOT AN AGENT'S: Run 5 disables the TPM, and on this firmware that removes the ppi directory that would re-enable it, so somebody has to be in firmware setup. Run 3 has no capsule. DO NOT DISPATCH A UNIT TO 'FINISH L-001' - there is nothing left an agent can do on this machine. NEW FINDINGS FROM ROUND 32, all landed: ppi/response reads '5 0: Success' the instant the request is written, before any reboot, so it proves nothing; the part returns TWO codes for a failed unseal and systemd prints ONE sentence for both (0x18b TPM_RC_HANDLE = the SRK at 0x81000001 is absent and is recoverable without re-enrolment because the SRK is deterministic from the storage seed; 0x1df TPM_RC_INTEGRITY = the seed was rolled and only re-enrolment works); systemd-cryptenroll provisions that SRK and systemd-cryptsetup never does, so an evicted SRK is a machine that refuses every TPM unlock at boot with the recovery key as the only way in; 'executing no operation' is a no-op on the LUKS HEADER ONLY - it persists a key at 0x81000001, a handle shared with every other OS on the machine - and the one-command re-enrolment trap is now measured after a REAL firmware clear, which is the case docs/boot-v2.md is actually about; a TPM clear moves PCR 1 PERMANENTLY on this board (three extra events in the firmware's own log, stable across a control reboot taken for that purpose) while PCR 0, 4 and 7 stay byte-identical across three boots. STILL TRUE FROM ROUND 31: systemd-pcrextend is a silent no-op on a GRUB machine and Secure Boot will NOT fix it; --tpm2-device=auto binds to no PCRs; a zero PCR 11 is a local DoS; DA is 32 tries / 2 h decay / 24 h recovery and a good auth does not clear the counter. EXACTLY THREE ROWS need redoing with Secure Boot ON and round 32 adds none: the --tpm2-pcrs=7 volume, the PCR 7 value itself, and the event-log replay.

units.title: The relay leg the Android app has never had — P1-060 C1s last piece
units.closed: CLOSED TO DISPATCH 2026-09-19 (round 33) -- landed as merge 2814f45d, 0 unlanded. THE RELAY LEG WORKS END TO END OVER THE REAL DEPLOYED RELAY, proven twice and independently: a hand-rolled Python guest (so the client under test was not also the witness) dialled wss://apex-relay.andrenijman.com and got HTTP/1.1 101, a matching accept value, {"relay":"paired"} and its hello byte spliced onto the daemon's listener; then a real Pixel 7a paired and ran a session through Cloudflare, device suite OK (35 tests), up from 32. The seam PairingService.kt:21 claimed turned out to be real, so no refactor was needed, and NO NEW DEPENDENCY was added -- argued rather than defaulted. WHAT IS LEFT IS A PERSON, NOT AN AGENT: the phone is still on the same Wi-Fi and takes the relay because the offer's LAN addresses were WITHHELD, not because they were unreachable. P1-051 was not touched and nothing this round bears on its remainder. FOUR DEFECTS WORTH REMEMBERING, all invisible to passing tests: SSLSocket does not verify the HOSTNAME by default (chain yes, name no), so without endpointIdentificationAlgorithm="HTTPS" the rendezvous id goes to whoever answers the address while every 'is TLS on?' test still passes; every relayed session leaked its socket because Session.close closes the streams and the adapters inherited a no-op close(); the Noise handshake on the relay leg ran with NO deadline despite a comment claiming otherwise; and four mutations into Relay.kt caught only two, one surviving because the parity assertion looked for a literal in the Rust source and compared it to nothing.

units.title: syft is SIGKILLed cataloguing the image — the last red step in build-image
units.closed: CLOSED TO DISPATCH 2026-09-20 (round 32) -- SOLVED AND VERIFIED, landed as merge b7e28d87. The SIGKILL was Go heap growth under the default GOGC=100 driving a 16 GB runner through memory and swap; GOMEMLIMIT=10GiB fixes it and syft is now PINNED to 1.52.0, which it was not -- it had been installing whatever main served, which would have left a measured fix protecting an unmeasured binary. Verified in a real build (run 35450175806): catalogued in 742 s, peak RSS 15,303,652 KB, 9830 packages, mem_avail never below ~4.7 GiB. THE NEGATIVE RESULTS ARE WORTH MORE THAN THE FIX, across eleven arms: the image SOURCE is irrelevant (oci-dir on local disk died identically to registry), so the fix previously preferred on this card addressed a non-cause; PARALLELISM is irrelevant (par 1 died the same), which means the timeout-death that justified raising the timeout to 45 minutes was ALSO a memory death, misread; the limit's VALUE is irrelevant (4, 6 and 10 GiB all peak at 14.65-14.80 GiB); swap adds nothing while the limit is set (32 GB bought 16 MB, 1 GB ever touched) and was deliberately not committed; swap WITHOUT the limit works badly (1958 s vs 904 s, 8.7M major faults). THE OOM-KILLER CLAIM IS LEFT CALIBRATED, not upgraded: oom_kill was 0 in every arm that lived to read it, so it has still never been read from a kernel message. The step now prints the counter delta, dmesg, peak RSS and the NAMED signal so the next death settles it. sbom-probe.yml is deleted; it answered its question. WHAT REMAINS IS A DIFFERENT PROBLEM and is unit sbom-attest: cosign gives up posting the ~166 MB predicate to Rekor.

units.title: Gaming Mode cannot release itself, and mangoapp fills /var with core dumps
units.closed: CLOSED TO DISPATCH 2026-09-19 (round 32) -- code done and landed as merge b76339cb. BOTH FIXES NEED AN IMAGE BUILD before anything is confirmed on hardware; the run-book rows are written (docs/gaming-and-sessions.md 6.6 and 6.7). The release fix is in apexd, the mangoapp fix in files/system/libexec/apex-gaming-session. RELEASE: apexd owns it now, not the session -- apex-gaming-session starts with an owner pid, apexd records the pid AND its /proc start time, and a 2 s watch calls the same idempotent game_exit when the owner is gone, emitting the same ActiveChanged/Status/TierChanged set a D-Bus exit emits so the shell does not keep showing a dead session. The polkit rule was DELIBERATELY NOT LOOSENED: allow_inactive is every local session, so loosening it would let any unprivileged user stop somebody else's Gaming Mode, and a SIGKILLed session runs no trap for a looser rule to permit anyway. MANGOAPP: diagnosed, not guessed. Core dump backtrace is XInternAtom from main with a NULL display; controlled headless A/B with the environment read out of /proc -- `--mangoapp` alone gives 0 restarts in 22 s, adding `--expose-wayland` gives 171. APEX passed both unconditionally, so the combination is ours. --expose-wayland STAYS (the hardware qualification was done with it and the overlay has never drawn a pixel); --mangoapp is gated on it, and APEX_GAMING_EXPOSE_WAYLAND=0 brings it back, which is what makes the gate testable both ways. THE 4 GB WAS NOT A MISSING BOUND -- MaxUse defaults to 10 percent of the filesystem CAPPED AT 4 GiB and katana's /var is 954 GB, so systemd's vacuum was working exactly as designed and 4 GiB is the wrong size for an ostree machine; the drop-in sets MaxUse=256M and KeepFree=2G. WHAT IS NOT A DISCRIMINATOR, and the run-book says so: katana's default AC tier is already `performance`, so the governor reads the same before, during and after -- use `active: false`, the apex-game cgroup being gone, sched_ext/state disabled, and apexd's `the session owner is gone` line instead. STILL UNCONFIRMED: that the MangoHud overlay actually RENDERS with expose-wayland off (it never has here), Safe Graphics' automatic dGPU branch, and any real game launch. RE-OPEN after an image build. || HARDWARE-CONFIRMED 2026-09-20 by unit integrated-image, and the RE-OPEN CONDITION IS SPENT. apex game status printed owner_pid 7799 matching bash /usr/libexec/apex-gaming-session. 6.6: THE RUN-BOOK'S OWN RECIPE DOES NOT TEST THIS ROW - `systemctl restart greetd` killed gamescope but the session script survived long enough to run its trap and released cleanly ('apexd game mode released', three times, idempotent). SIGKILLing the owner is what 'nothing can cooperate' has to mean, and then apexd fired 1.9 s later: 'game: the session owner is gone (/proc/9688 is gone) - releasing game mode. Nothing else could'. active false, apex-game cgroup removed, no gamescope left. The run-book should be amended. 6.7: gamescope starts --expose-wayland and WITHOUT --mangoapp with the explanation printed; 0 new mangoapp dumps against 15376 in one boot, 0 Glfw Error lines against 57612, 171 session journal lines against 144187, MaxUse=256M KeepFree=2G live. greetd restored byte-identical, 0 timers. NOT confirmed and not claimed: the overlay RENDERING with APEX_GAMING_EXPOSE_WAYLAND=0, Safe Graphics' dGPU branch, any real game. AND A NEW DEFECT: sched_ext/state is NOT a discriminator here either, because apexd runs `scxctl switch -s scx_lavd` where the machine needs `scxctl start` (scxctl says so verbatim) - so Gaming Mode has NEVER loaded a sched-ext scheduler, on this image or the previous two, while apex game status's notes field claims it did. apexd/apexd-core/src/syswriter.rs:739. Wants its own unit. Evidence integrated-image-20260920.md sections 6 and 7.

units.title: cosign cannot post the SBOM attestation to Rekor
units.closed: CLOSED 2026-09-20 (round 32) -- SOLVED, VERIFIED AND LANDED as merge 97c9e8f2. The whole image job is green for the first time, INCLUDING the two steps that had been skipped and therefore unproved in every failing run: promoting the published tags and asserting they all resolve to this digest. REKOR WAS NOT RETURNING 413 AND THE CEILING IS NOT 16 MB. Sixteen direct posts at ascending sizes, each retested: at or below 25,000,092 B Rekor answers 400 having FULLY PROCESSED the body; at or above 25,165,916 B it answers 502 with size_upload=0 in ~0.43 s, refused by the fronting proxy on Content-Length before a byte is sent. The boundary brackets 24 MiB exactly and was re-confirmed from a GitHub runner. That also explains the message: 502 is in go-retryablehttp's RETRYABLE class, so cosign retried a refusal that can never succeed and said `giving up after 4 attempt(s)` -- structurally incapable of naming its cause -- and size_upload=0 is why four attempts fit in 3.86 s. CHOSEN: trim the predicate, KEEP the transparency log. Published is the complete package inventory (9830 packages, every version, 9830 purls, 55,652 CPEs, both Electron trees); file rows and the 16,463-edge dependency graph are dropped. Same signature, same keyless identity, same spdxjson type, same public Rekor entry. The cost is in docs/trust-enforcement.md: the SBOM is a flat list and no longer says which files are in the image -- structure, reproducible from the published digest with one syft run, where identity is not reproducible from anything smaller. THE OCI-ARTEFACT OPTION WOULD HAVE BEEN ACTIVELY HARMFUL: verify.rs:540 requires predicateType to contain spdx, and a FAILED provenance check is refused even at provenance=warn, so it would have refused updates on every machine in the field. DO NOT, per the unit's own warning: tighten provenance=warn to enforce, or edit the `no published APEX image has an SBOM attestation yet` sentences in docs/ or verify.rs. Both are STILL TRUE -- this was a task branch and the PUBLISH guard moved no tracked tag. They belong to the first green main build. THREE THINGS THAT COST REAL TIME, recorded so they do not again: SYFT_FILE_METADATA_SELECTION=none is NOT the lever (13%, not 64%) and does not reduce RSS; `local a="$1" b="${a}"` is an unbound-variable error under set -u and threw away 915 s; and a workflow `run:` block is capped at 21,000 characters, which surfaces as a JOBLESS FAILED RUN, not a failing step.

units.title: apex install mislabels every /etc file it writes, silently, with no AVC
units.closed: CLOSED 2026-09-20 (round 33) -- fixed and landed as merge 661a9d80. install_etc collects every path it creates or overwrites AS IT GOES and hands the list to `restorecon -F -i -f`, so the label comes from the LOADED POLICY instead of from `cp -a` preserving the extraction tree's rpm_var_lib_t. Each branch records only what it actually wrote; a directory is recorded only when WE create it, because mkdir inherits the parent's type (wrong for e.g. /etc/cron.d -> system_cron_spool_t); the removal pass records survivors no installed package owns, which is the class the katana leftover belonged to. `-F` IS LOAD-BEARING: a bare restorecon silently DECLINES any type in the policy's customizable_types list, says `not reset as customized by admin`, and still exits 0. stderr is deliberately not swallowed -- this defect reported nothing for months, so a fix that could also report nothing would not be one. `label_tree` is untouched ON PURPOSE: split_out_of_image has already moved /etc out of the payload root before it runs. SELF-HEALING SIDE EFFECT: because the pass relabels tracked paths it declines to delete, the next `apex install` or `apex update` repairs a machine that already carries the mislabel. THE GATE asserts the property over EVERYTHING the pass writes, never over .pwd.lock (only where it bit). Real packages decide which paths exist, a before/after CTIME snapshot decides which the pass touched (a directory counts only when new, because a dir's ctime moves when a child lands in it), and the engine runs TWICE because the SECOND install is the overwrite that broke katana. Enforced 21/0; coverage-forced 9/0 which is the CI floor. Every control fires, including a pre-fix replica reproducing the katana finding exactly (58 files wrong). The suite REFUSES TO DEGRADE SILENTLY: a host with /sys/fs/selinux/enforce that does not run the enforced leg is a FAIL, not a skip. CI floor is 9 because ubuntu-24.04 has no SELinux AND podman's rootfs is mounted `context=` where setxattr security.selinux is EOPNOTSUPP. THE SUITE HAS NEVER RUN ON AN UBUNTU RUNNER -- if that job goes red, read PROBE_MODE/PROBE_CAPABILITY first. ONLY A REAL MACHINE CAN CONFIRM: that a DynamicUser unit starts after an install (no PID 1 in a container), that restorecon resolves against APEX's loaded policy rather than Fedora 43's policy rpm, and that the extraction tree comes out rpm_var_lib_t on its own (the suite chcons it to reproduce katana exactly).

units.title: Gaming Mode never loads a scheduler, and status claims it did
units.closed: CLOSED 2026-09-20 (round 33) -- fixed and landed as merge faa1992d. scxctl has TWO verbs and they are not interchangeable: `start` attaches when none is running, `switch` replaces one that is, and each REFUSES in the other's state. APEX loads nothing at boot so the first entry always finds none, and the code hardcoded `switch`. Swapping in `start` would have been the same mistake spelled differently -- correct on every machine APEX ships today, wrong on any machine already running a scheduler. The verb is now READ off /sys/kernel/sched_ext/state with one retry on whichever verb the loader's own error names; both refusal strings came out of the shipped scxctl 1.1.2 binary, not guesswork. THE STATUS WAS THE EXPENSIVE HALF: scxctl exiting 0 is a fact about scxctl. The writer now waits (bounded, 2 s) and reports what it read from the KERNEL. `not loaded` keeps its cause -- scxctl refused, or scxctl exited 0 and the kernel still reads disabled (the general form of this defect), or no CONFIG_SCHED_CLASS_EXT (a DEFINITE answer, not an unknown). `unknown` is only an unreadable state or one caught mid-transition, never rounded to either neighbour. Outcome gained a third variant because two could not hold `I could not tell`. SIBLING AUDIT, same shape next door: gpus_locked was cloned from the plan while run_nvidia_smi's refusal went unread, so a GPU whose lock was REJECTED was reported as locked; and game_exit discarded every outcome but a hard Err, so a refused restore was silent under a line asserting the machine had been put back. Both fixed. TWO DOCUMENTS CLAIMED KATANA RAN scx_lavd FOR 75 MINUTES. Nothing was running. Corrected in place and marked as corrections. RUN-BOOK: the `sched_ext/state expect: enabled` row is DELETED -- it read disabled throughout, so it passed on a file that never moved; the 6.6 destroy step is now `kill -9` the owner, because a greetd restart leaves the script alive to run its own trap and was testing the cooperative path; governor and sched-ext are now a named PAIR of non-discriminators on katana. ONE MUTATION ESCAPED THE FIRST PASS (MB11): nothing pinned the plan-time note, so restoring the sentence that had claimed a scheduler on three images turned nothing red -- a gate that inspects nothing, inside the work fixing a gate that inspects nothing. Two assertions added, caught both ways; the near-miss is in the evidence. KNOWN AND STATED: game mode STOPS a scheduler it found running rather than restoring it (`scxctl restore` would be the fix); that branch has never been reached. Three rows in 6.8 need hardware, including the `switch` branch a fixture cannot honestly stand in for.
